findings.comment: recordClubBulk reads the mirrored buyerID column unconditionally to find who already bought a set, but the column is only populated on save and may be null for rows written before the backfill. When the read switch is off and mirror rows remain null, buyers are not skipped, so the function inserts a club unread row for a set they already own and the bought set shows NEW on the club tab instead of purchased. Gate the lookup on the read switch and fall back to userID.

finding_contract.current_impact: Buyers of a club set still receive a club unread row while the mirror column is unpopulated, so the club tab shows NEW for a set they bought.
finding_contract.falsifiable_condition: Publish a set to a member whose purchase row has a null buyerID.
finding_contract.expected_observable: The member gets a club unread row for the bought set.
finding_contract.uncertainty: Whether any null rows remain is not visible from the code.

findings.comment: The parentTeam mapping keys on .id while the team mapping uses the identifier (.databaseId // .id) | tostring, so in a payload shape where .id is the node id the two mappings key the same teams by different identifiers and parent links stop resolving. Use the same identifier expression in both mappings.

finding_contract.current_impact: No impact today: the payload shape in use carries the numeric id in .id, so both mappings key the same teams the same way.
finding_contract.counterfactual_trigger: A payload shape where .id is the node id.
finding_contract.falsifiable_condition: Sync a team from a GraphQL-shaped payload.
finding_contract.expected_observable: The parent link points at an identifier no entity uses.
finding_contract.uncertainty: Depends on the payload shape the integration sends.
